questions.question: The ratio of selling price to the cost price is 9 ∶ 8. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price (S.P) : Cost price (C.P) = 9 : 8

**Formula used:**

Profit% = {(S.P - C.P) × 100}/C.P

**Calculation:**

Profit% = {(S.P - C.P) × 100}/C.P

⇒ {(9 - 8) × 100}/8

⇒ {1 × 100}/8 = 12.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5%.**

questions.question: Simple interest on a sum for eight months at the rate of 8 percent per annum is Rs. 240. What is the value of sum?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective interest rate for 8 months = 8 × (8 ÷ 12) = 16/3%

As per the question, (16/3)% of Sum = 240

1% of Sum = (240 × 3) ÷ 16 = 45

100% of Sum = 45 × 100 = 4500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) = ₹240

Rate (R) = 8% per annum

Time (T) = 8 months = 8 ÷ 12 = 2/3 years

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3001218e0d1d066e9605cbecfac6d5c89364ef5509afcf5e52c11bb3bafbcb79.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 240 = [P × 8 × (2 ÷ 3)] ÷ 100

⇒ 240 = (P × 16) ÷ 300

⇒ P = (240 × 300) ÷ 16

⇒ P = 15 × 300

⇒ P = 4500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total amount (A) at the end of the time period is given by: A = P + SI, where P is the Principal and SI is the Simple Interest.

Effective Interest Rate

The overall interest rate accumulated over T years is simply (R × T)%. So, SI = (R × T)% of Principal.

Time Conversion

When time is given in months, divide by 12 to convert it to years (e.g., 8 months = 8 ÷ 12 years). If given in days, divide by 365.

Difference Between SI and CI

In Simple Interest, the principal remains constant. In Compound Interest (CI), interest is calculated on both the initial principal and the accumulated interest.

questions.question: P and Q start from the same point and at the same time with speeds 20 km/hr and 16 km/hr respectively. What is the distance between P and Q after 4 hours if both move in same direction?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When two objects move in the **same direction**, their **Relative Speed** is the difference between their individual speeds.

**Relative Speed** = 20 km/hr − 16 km/hr = 4 km/hr.

**Distance** = Relative Speed × Time

⇒ Distance = 4 km/hr × 4 hr = 16 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 km.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of **P** (SP) = 20 km/hr

Speed of **Q** (SQ) = 16 km/hr

**Time** (T) = 4 hr

**Formula Used:** Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/70e973f92bd5b86aa268189681f19fd8c002de3ad3ea7758afe1fa4494caef8e.png] 

⇒ Distance covered by **P** in 4 hr = 20 × 4 = 80 km.

⇒ Distance covered by **Q** in 4 hr = 16 × 4 = 64 km.

⇒ Required **Distance between P and Q** = Distance of P − Distance of Q

⇒ Distance = 80 km − 64 km = 16 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 km.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction at speeds u and v ( v), the relative speed is (u − v).

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move in opposite directions at speeds u and v, the relative speed is (u + v).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Distance Constant Rule

If distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1/T).</p

questions.question: A mixture of 500 litres of alcohol and water contains 20 percent water. How much more water should be added to this so that the water will become 50 percent in the new mixture?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since **Alcohol** quantity remains **constant**:

Initial Alcohol % × Initial Total Volume = Final Alcohol % × Final Total Volume

80% × 500 = 50% × New Total Volume

New Total Volume = (80 × 500) ÷ 50 = 800 litres

Water added = 800 − 500 = 300 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 300 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial mixture = 500 litres, Initial water % = 20%, Required water % = 50%.

**Formula Used:** Quantity of constant substance = Total Volume × Concentration %

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6b184716179a8ce489f06059bbc5fff5c1016d0d6cabc2c5a4802f6c7a6767ad.png] 

⇒ Initial Water = 20% of 500 = 100 litres

⇒ Initial Alcohol = 500 − 100 = 400 litres

⇒ Let **x** litres of water be added.

⇒ New Total Volume = 500 + x

⇒ New Alcohol % = 50%

⇒ Since only water is added, Alcohol remains 400 litres.

⇒ 50% of (500 + x) = 400

⇒ (1/2) × (500 + x) = 400

⇒ 500 + x = 800

⇒ x = 300 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 300 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Quantity Concept

In mixture problems where only one component is added or removed, the quantity of the other component remains constant (V₁ × C₁ = V₂ × C₂).

Alligation Method

Can be used by taking water concentration: (Initial 20%) and (Added Water 100%) to get (Final 50%). Ratio of Initial : Added = (100−50) : (50−20) = 50 : 30 = 5 : 3.

Percentage to Ratio Conversion

20% water means Alcohol:Water = 4:1. 50% water means Alcohol:Water = 1:1. Equating alcohol parts (making them 4:4), the water change is 1 to 4 units (3 units increase).</p
